🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
This month

The Autumn Edit

October is a build month. Two glute sessions, one capped-shoulders and triceps session and one back, rear-delt and biceps session give the week a clear shape, with four different ten-minute ab blocks layered in without turning every workout into endless volume.

This Month's Focus

Train hard enough to progress, not hard enough to ruin recovery. Keep the main lifts controlled, write down your weights and reps, and use the home mirror whenever life gets in the way of the gym.

What To Expect

Heavy hip thrusts, unilateral glute work, capped-shoulder volume, back-width work and four simple core styles: weighted, bodyweight, cable-loaded and plank/stability.

How This Training Supports Your Goal

The same four sessions repeat through the month so you can improve them. Week 1 sets your baseline. By Week 4, aim to beat one lower-body lift and one upper-body lift with a rep, a small load increase, better range or cleaner control.

Kassy’s training note

Do not chase soreness. Track the lifts that matter, keep 1–2 good reps in reserve on most working sets and make your form look better before you make the weight bigger.

🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
Your plan

How to follow + choose your goal

Fat Loss Foundation

3–4 workouts per week.

Complete the warm-up or activation and the main workout. The ten-minute abs and finisher are optional extras.

Keep the main lifts challenging with roughly 1–2 reps in reserve. Strength holding steady while dieting is a win.

If you only have three sessions, keep both glute days and alternate the two upper-body days week to week.

Balanced Toning

4 workouts per week.

Complete the warm-up, main workout and the paired ten-minute abs. Add the finisher when you are recovering well.

Progress one variable at a time: weight, reps, range, tempo or control.

Glute Growth

4–5 workouts per week.

Complete the full four-day plan including abs and finishers. Add a fifth session only when sleep, food, performance and soreness all say recovery is good.

For an optional fifth session, repeat Workout 1 or Workout 3 and alternate which lower-body day you repeat from week to week.

Do not add upper-body volume if it costs you glute recovery.

The rule

Main compound lifts: usually 90–120 seconds rest.

Accessories: usually 60–90 seconds rest.

Finishers: use the written rest.

Add weight when you can hit the top of the rep range across all sets with clean form.

🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
Build through the month

Progression

Week 1

Learn the order, choose clean starting loads and log every main lift.

Week 2

Add a rep where you can or make the lowering phase more controlled.

Week 3

Add a small load increase, extra range or stronger band tension on one or two movements.

Week 4

Keep form clean and beat Week 1 on one lower-body and one upper-body lift.

Your progress check

Compare Week 1 with Week 4 on one lower-body and one upper-body lift.

LiftWeek 1Week 4
Lower-body lift
Upper-body lift

Core - form

Ribs down. Exhale as you crunch. On reverse-crunch and leg-raise work, curl the pelvis rather than swinging the legs. If your lower back lifts, shorten the lever. The plan deliberately avoids loads of twisting and side-bending.

10
🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
Progression, swaps & form

Glutes: swaps + form

Glutes - swaps

  • Barbell hip thrust → hip-thrust machine / dumbbell hip thrust / sofa hip thrust.
  • B-stance RDL → dumbbell B-stance RDL / standard RDL.
  • Deficit curtsy lunge → standard curtsy lunge / glute-biased reverse lunge if curtsies do not suit you.
  • Single-leg leg press → high step-up / supported split squat.
  • Cable kickback → banded kickback.
  • 45° glute-biased hyperextension → single-leg glute bridge / banded hip extension.
  • Side cable abduction → standing band abduction.

Glutes - form

Ribs down, chin tucked on thrusts and finish with the glutes rather than the lower back. On hinges, push the hips back and stop where your hamstrings stop. On unilateral work, keep the working foot planted and move slowly enough to own the bottom position.

Main compound lifts: usually 90–120 seconds rest. Accessories: usually 60–90 seconds rest. Finishers: use the written rest. Add weight when you can hit the top of the rep range across all sets with clean form.

11
🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
Progression, swaps & form

Upper body: swaps + form

Shoulders + Triceps - swaps

  • Seated DB overhead press → machine shoulder press / half-kneeling single-arm press.
  • Cable lateral raise → dumbbell lateral raise / long-band lateral raise.
  • Incline machine chest press → incline DB press / feet-elevated press-up.
  • Reverse pec deck → bent-over DB rear-delt fly.
  • Rope face pull → band face pull.
  • Rope pushdown → band pushdown / overhead DB extension.

Shoulders + Triceps - form

Lead with the elbows on raises and keep the traps quiet. Keep ribs stacked on overhead presses. On triceps work, pin the upper arm and let the elbow do the moving.

Back + Biceps - swaps

  • Pull-ups → assisted pull-ups / door-anchored band pulldown.
  • Single-arm DB row → chest-supported row / one-arm cable row.
  • Wide-grip lat pulldown → wide band pulldown.
  • Single-arm cable row → one-arm DB row / band row.
  • Straight-arm cable pulldown → band straight-arm pulldown / DB pullover.
  • Incline DB curl → seated long-lever curl if no incline bench.

Back + Biceps - form

Think elbows toward hips on lat work, keep the chest proud and avoid shrugging. On curls, keep the elbow still and control the lowering phase.

🍒The Model Body ClubThe Autumn Edit
Gym workout 01

Glutes

Glute growth + shapeSwitch to home version →

Warm-Up · 5 Min

2 rounds

Banded Lateral Walks — 15 steps each way

Frog Pumps — 20

Banded Glute Bridges — 15

Standing Band Abduction — 12 each side

Keep it light. The warm-up should switch the glutes on, not tire them out.

Main Workout

Rest 90–120 sec on hip thrusts and RDLs; 60–90 sec on the rest.

1. Barbell Hip Thrust4 × 6–10

Cue: Squeeze your glutes for 1–2 seconds at the top.

2. B-Stance Barbell RDL3 × 8–10 each side

Cue: Lower slowly and feel the stretch through the working glute.

3. Deficit Curtsy Lunge3 × 10–12 each side

Cue: Take a long stride and control the depth.

4. Single-Leg Leg Press3 × 10–12 each side

Cue: Place your foot slightly higher and drive through your heel.

5. Cable Kickback3 × 12–15 each side

Cue: Kick slightly backwards and outwards.

6. 45° Glute-Biased Hyperextension3 × 10–15

Cue: Finish by squeezing your glutes, not extending your lower back.

Fat Loss Foundation ends here.

Core

WEIGHTED ABS · 10 MIN

45 sec work / 15 sec changeover

Complete 2 rounds.

Use one dumbbell or weight plate throughout.

1. Weighted Crunch

Hold the weight at your chest and curl your shoulders off the floor.

2. Weighted Dead Bug

Hold the weight above your chest while alternating slow leg extensions.

3. Weighted Toe Reach

Legs straight up, hold the weight overhead and reach towards your toes.

4. Weighted Reverse Crunch

Hold the weight above your chest and curl your hips up towards your ribs.

5. Weighted Crunch Hold + Pulses

Hold the top of a crunch and perform short controlled pulses.

Make it harder: use a weight that makes the final 10–15 seconds difficult without losing control.

Balanced Toning ends here.

Finisher

ABDUCTION MECHANICAL DROP

2–3 rounds

Lean-Forward Abduction — 15 reps

Upright Abduction — 15 reps

Partials — 20 reps

Rest 45–60 sec between rounds.

Cue: Keep constant tension on your upper glutes.

Glute Growth ends here.
Completed

Gym workout 02

Capped Shoulders + Triceps

Shoulder shape + arm definitionSwitch to home version →

Warm-Up

2 rounds

Press-Ups — 10

Band Pull-Aparts — 15

Band External Rotations — 12

Rest 20–30 sec between rounds.

Main Workout

Rest 90–120 sec after overhead press; 60–75 sec on accessories.

1. Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press4 × 6–10

Cue: Press overhead without shrugging your shoulders.

2. Seated Lateral Raise4 × 10–15

Cue: Lead with your elbows and control every rep.

Last set: partials to failure with clean positioning.

3. Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise3 × 12–15 each side

Cue: Sweep your arm out to the side and keep your trap relaxed.

4. Incline Machine Chest Press3 × 8–12

Cue: Keep the bench inclined and drive through your upper chest.

5. Reverse Pec Deck / Rear-Delt Fly4 × 12–15

Cue: Lead with your elbows rather than pulling with your back.

6. Seated Rope Face Pull3 × 12–15

Cue: Pull the rope towards eye level with your elbows high.

7. Tricep Rope Pushdown3 × 10–15

Cue: Keep your elbows pinned and fully straighten your arms.

Fat Loss Foundation ends here.

Core

BODYWEIGHT ABS · 10 MIN

45 sec work / 15 sec changeover

Complete 2 rounds.

1. Reverse Crunch

Curl your pelvis off the floor rather than swinging your legs.

2. Straight-Leg Raise

Lower your legs slowly and stop before your lower back lifts.

3. Crunch

Exhale hard as you curl your ribs towards your pelvis.

4. Dead Bug

Alternate opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back pressed down.

5. Hollow Body Hold

Shoulders and legs lifted. Keep your lower back firmly against the floor.

Make it harder: make every lowering phase about 3 seconds rather than rushing the reps.

Balanced Toning ends here.

Finisher

LATERAL RAISE BURNOUT

2 rounds

10 full reps → 10 partials → 10-second hold

Rest 45 sec between rounds.

Cue: Keep your shoulders down and maintain tension throughout.

Glute Growth ends here.
Completed

Gym workout 03

Glutes 2

Glute strength + unilateral controlSwitch to home version →

Warm-Up

2 rounds

Banded Glute Bridge — 15

Banded Good Morning — 15

Lateral Walk — 15 each way

Frog Pumps — 20

Rest only as needed.

Main Workout

Rest 90–120 sec on thrusts, RDLs and split squats; 60–90 sec on accessories.

1. Kas Hip Thrust Machine4 × 8–10

Cue: Keep the range short and squeeze hard at the top.

2. Romanian Deadlift3–4 × 8–10

Cue: Push your hips backwards and keep the dumbbells or bar close.

3. Bulgarian Split Squat3 × 8–10 each leg

Cue: Take a longer stance and lean slightly forward for more glute.

4. B-Stance Hip Thrust3 × 10–12 each side

Cue: Let the working glute do most of the work.

5. 45° Hyperextension3 × 12–15

Cue: Round slightly through the upper back and squeeze your glutes to finish.

6. Kneeling Cable Kickback3 × 12–15 each side

Cue: Drive your heel back without arching your lower back.

Fat Loss Foundation ends here.

Core

CABLE CRUNCH ABS · 10 MIN

45 sec work / 15 sec changeover

Complete 2 rounds.

Use a rope attachment on a high cable.

1. Kneeling Cable Crunch

Curl ribs towards pelvis. Do not just hinge at the hips.

2. Kneeling Cable Crunch + Pause

Same movement but hold the bottom position for 2 seconds every rep.

3. Hanging Knee Raise

Curl your pelvis upwards at the top rather than simply lifting your knees.

4. Kneeling Cable Crunch Pulses

Stay in the bottom half of the crunch and perform controlled pulses.

5. Hanging Leg Raise

Keep legs as straight as you can and control the lowering phase.

Make it harder: increase the cable weight slightly for round two while keeping every rep slow.

Balanced Toning ends here.

Finisher

SIDE CABLE ABDUCTION

3 × 15–20 each side

After the final full-rep set, add 20 controlled partials each side.

Rest 45–60 sec between sets.

Cue: Lead with your heel and keep the movement controlled.

Glute Growth ends here.

Gym workout 04

Back + Rear Delts + Biceps

Back width + arm definitionSwitch to home version →

Warm-Up

2 rounds

Band Pull-Aparts — 15

Straight-Arm Band Pulldowns — 12

Scapular Pull-Ups or Scapular Depressions — 8–10

Rest 20–30 sec between rounds.

Main Workout

Rest 90–120 sec on pull-ups; 60–90 sec on rows and pulldowns; 60 sec on curls and rear delts.

1. Pull-Ups5 × 6–10

Cue: Drive your elbows down towards your hips.

Use assistance if needed to stay inside the rep range with clean form.

2. Single-Arm Dumbbell Row4 × 8–12 each side

Cue: Pull the dumbbell back towards your hip.

3. Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown3 × 10–12

Cue: Pull your elbows down and slightly out.

4. Single-Arm Cable Row3 × 10–12 each side

Cue: Keep your elbow tucked and pull towards your hip.

5. Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown3 × 12–15

Cue: Sweep your hands down towards your thighs.

6. Cable Rear-Delt Fly3 × 15–20

Cue: Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down.

7. Incline Dumbbell Curl3 × 10–12

Cue: Keep your elbows still and lower slowly.

Fat Loss Foundation ends here.

Core

PLANK ABS · 10 MIN

45 sec work / 15 sec changeover

Complete 2 rounds.

1. Forearm Plank

Keep ribs tucked, squeeze glutes and pull your belly button in.

2. Plank Knee Drives

From high plank, slowly drive alternate knees towards your chest.

3. Plank Body Saws

From forearm plank, rock your body slowly forwards and backwards.

4. High Plank Knee-To-Elbow

Bring one knee forwards towards the same-side elbow, alternating sides.

5. Long-Lever Plank

Place your forearms slightly further forwards than a normal plank. Hold and brace hard.

Make it harder: actively pull your elbows towards your toes during every plank hold.

Balanced Toning ends here.

Finisher

DUMBBELL SUPERSET · 3 ROUNDS

A. Dumbbell Hammer Curl — 10–12 reps

Cue: Keep your elbows tucked and do not swing.

Straight into:

B. Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear-Delt Fly — 15–20 reps

Cue: Raise the dumbbells out wide without shrugging.

Rest 45 seconds after each round.

Glute Growth ends here.

The Autumn Edit

Keep going

The Autumn Edit is about making progress easy to see. Keep the four workout numbers the same whether you train at home or in the gym, log the main lifts and let the month build instead of changing the plan every week.

By Week 4, compare with Week 1

  • One lower-body lift improved.
  • One upper-body lift improved.
  • Your home version saved at least one session you might otherwise have skipped.
  • Your abs got four genuinely different training styles across the week.

Pair this plan with the October meal plan and use the same seven-day challenge across both. You only need to run the challenge once.

Lots of love,
Kassy
